items.title: CVE-2026-115407
items.summary: In github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2 versions <= 2.0.0-rc8 (and the deprecated v1 module paths github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8, github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1 and github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5), the cipher.AEAD returned by SecretKey.NewGCM() passes whatever nonce it is given straight to CK_GCM_PARAMS without checking its length against NonceSize(), and accepts an empty nonce. On a token that accepts a zero-length GCM IV — SoftHSM2 does — every Seal with an empty nonce encrypts under the same IV, reusing the keystream and exposing the GHASH authentication key, which allows forgeries. Separately, Config.UseGCMIVFromHSM sends a NULL IV with length zero to the token unless GCMIVFromHSMControl.SupplyIvForHSMGCMEncrypt is also set, so the token has nowhere to write the IV it generates: a Seal with a non-empty nonce panics after the plaintext has already been encrypted, and a Seal with an empty nonce returns ciphertext under an empty IV without error. On the v1 line HSM-IV mode additionally never copies the token-generated IV back to the caller, so the caller keeps its own nonce while the data was encrypted under another one.

items.title: CVE-2026-132660
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), several SECURITY DEFINER functions in the pem schema of the PEM backend database are owned by a superuser but do not set a safe search_path. Any PEM user who can connect to the PEM backend database can create objects that these functions use in place of the intended ones, and so run arbitrary SQL with superuser privileges. Temporary objects can be used for this on every supported PostgreSQL version, and objects in the public schema on PostgreSQL 14 backends and backends upgraded from PostgreSQL 14. From PEM 10.6.1, these functions run with a fixed search_path.

items.title: CVE-2026-132659
items.summary: In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the row-level security policies on pem.job and pem.jobstep that apply to PEM agents do not limit an agent to its own jobs. An attacker who controls one monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can create, change or delete jobs for every other agent, including the agent on the PEM server. Agents run SQL job steps with the database credentials of the server they monitor, and shell job steps where batch jobs are enabled, so compromising one monitored host can give superuser SQL access to every monitored database and to the PEM backend. From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents can no longer create jobs or change job definitions or job steps.

items.title: CVE-2026-80188: BuddyBoss Addons <= 1.2.1 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via Unverified Social Login Identity Tokens
items.summary: The BuddyBoss Addons plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in versions up to, and including, 1.2.1. This is due to the Social Login REST endpoint trusting unverified Apple and Facebook identity-token claims and linking an attacker-controlled provider identifier to an existing WordPress user selected by the token’s email claim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know a user’s email address to associate their provider identity with that account, including administrator accounts, and subsequently authenticate as the victim. Successful exploitation requires the BuddyBoss Platform plugin to be installed and active, with the Social Login module and selected provider enabled and configured. On sites with the separate BuddyBoss App JWT component, the vulnerable REST request can return an application token immediately.

items.title: CVE-2026-101340: Query ID predictable from a short sequence of observations
items.summary: Net::DNS uses a 16-bit query ID to match responses to the corresponding requests. In versions up to and including 1.57, the ID is obtained from Perl's built-in rand() function. An attacker that can observe the sequence of query IDs is able to expose the internal state of the PNRG and hence predict query IDs before they are transmitted. The victim Net::DNS instance is then exposed to forged responses injected by the attacker. Note that the deduplication cache in 1.57 has no impact on the feasibility of this attack.

items.title: CVE-2026-133648: Flowintel Disables TLS Certificate Verification for MISP and Mail Connections
items.summary: Flowintel disabled TLS certificate verification for all MISP API connections and used unverified SSL contexts for IMAP and SMTP STARTTLS mail connections. This allowed an on-path (man-in-the-middle) attacker positioned between Flowintel and its MISP or mail servers to impersonate the remote server and intercept sensitive data. Affected connections include: All MISP HTTPS API calls (event retrieval, attribute search, event creation, connectivity checks, and API validation) SMTP STARTTLS connections used for sending email notifications IMAP TLS connections used for fetching mail archives and testing connectivity An attacker who can observe or intercept network traffic between Flowintel and the MISP or mail server could: Capture MISP API keys and mail credentials (SMTP/IMAP passwords) Read all threat intelligence data exchanged (events, attributes, objects, reports) Inject or modify threat intelligence data returned to Flowintel The vulnerability required no authentication on the part of the attacker and no user interaction; it was exploitable by any party with a network position between Flowintel and its configured MISP or mail endpoints. Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

items.title: CVE-2026-77312: Flyto2 Core: Arbitrary file write via unguarded data.*/file.* modules (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-67429)
items.summary: Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, the earlier CVE-2026-67429 remediation applied validate_path_with_env_config() to only a hand-picked set of file-writing modules, leaving data.csv.write in src/core/modules/atomic/data/csv_write.py, data.json_to_csv in src/core/modules/atomic/data/json_to_csv.py, file.copy in src/core/modules/atomic/file/copy.py, and file.move in src/core/modules/atomic/file/move.py outside the FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR confinement boundary. A caller able to execute modules or recipes can therefore write attacker-controlled content outside the configured sandbox, potentially overwriting application code, recipes, startup files, scheduled-task files, or authorization files and gaining code execution on the host. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

From 1.8.14 until 3.3.3, the pre-authentication /static/* plugin asset handler in src/node/utils/Minify.ts performs a backslash-to-forward-slash conversion after src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts has completed its POSIX path checks. On POSIX systems the sanitizer correctly treats backslashes as ordinary filename bytes, but the later conversion turns encoded backslash-separated parent-directory segments into traversal components without revalidation or containment. The expressPreSession registration and the always-present ep_etherpad-lite core pseudo-plugin make this path reachable without credentials, allowing a remote attacker to read any file available to the Etherpad process. Disclosed configuration or environment secrets can expose administrator credentials, after which the administrator plugin installer can provide in-process code execution and full server compromise. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.3.

items.title: CVE-2026-104099: Fabio: Access-control bypass through unnormalized request paths
items.summary: Fabio is an HTTP(S) and TCP router for deploying applications managed by consul. Prior to 1.7.3, route/table.go selects targets using raw req.URL.Path, while proxy/http_proxy.go applies per-route ACL and basic-auth checks to the selected target and forwards the raw path to the origin. Dot-segment, encoded-dot, or repeated-slash variants can fall through to a less restrictive route that reaches the same backend; the backend then normalizes the path and serves the protected resource without the configured access controls. A less restrictive fallback route must reach the same backend; without one, the request returns 404. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.3.

items.title: CVE-2026-77359: Jupyter MCP Server: Browser DNS rebinding can hijack the Jupyter backend through management routes
items.summary: Jupyter MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for Jupyter. Prior to 1.0.3, standalone streamable-http mode validates Host and Origin values for /mcp but does not apply the same browser-origin controls to the state-changing /api/connect and /api/stop management routes. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding so that its hostname resolves to a loopback, LAN, VPN, or published-container MCP listener, then send a browser-shaped request that /api/connect accepts to replace runtime_url and document_url values and start a kernel client against attacker-controlled infrastructure. The attacker can thereby cause Jupyter API and WebSocket traffic to reach that infrastructure and can use /api/stop to stop the current notebook kernel. The default broad bind can increase exposure, but the vulnerability is the missing management-route origin boundary, not a lack of Host validation on /mcp. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.3.

items.title: CVE-2026-129496: Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution
items.summary: Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution. items.title: CVE-2026-120753: Eclipse Ditto gateway accepts `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` from a URL query parameter, allowing unauthenticated subject impersonation (default Helm chart)
items.summary: In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the x-ditto-pre-authenticated HTTP header set by a trusted reverse proxy, but also from an undocumented x-ditto-pre-authenticated URL query parameter that a client can set. A reverse proxy that only overwrites the header therefore does not stop clients from supplying their own subject. With the default configuration of the Ditto Helm chart (global.jwtOnly: false, which implicitly enables pre-authentication), the bundled nginx skips HTTP Basic authentication for any request with an Authorization: Bearer header and forwards it without the pre-authentication header. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an invalid Bearer token together with the query parameter to authenticate as any chosen policy subject. Pre-authentication succeeds before the JWT is validated, so the attacker can read and modify Things and Policies with that subject's permissions. As a mitigation, disable pre-authentication in the gateway (ENABLE_PRE_AUTHENTICATION=false) or, when using the Helm chart, configure global.jwtOnly: true.

items.summary: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms. Prior to 6.2.1, AnsibleForms uses a public hard-coded fallback JWT signing secret from server/config/auth.config.js when ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET is unset. items.summary: Miren Runtime provides the runtime component for the Miren application platform. Prior to 0.11.1, the QUIC/HTTP3 RPC server on the default port 8443 uses tls.RequestClientCert and does not verify that presented certificates chain to the configured cluster certificate authority. The RPC authenticators derive a caller identity from PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName without requiring a non-empty VerifiedChains value, and certificate identities bypass all RBAC checks. A network attacker who can reach the listener can present a self-signed certificate with an issuer distinguished name matching the public cluster CA subject and gain cluster superuser access, allowing disclosure, modification, or disruption of applications, sandboxes, disks, credentials, and other managed resources. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.1.
